cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Approve the Harmless Version
cards.instruction: Get approval for a harmless version of your plan, then gradually reveal what that approval now commits them to.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll keep the hall clear. Can I add one chair beside the noticeboard?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I'll chair the tenants' meeting from it. Could you bring yours out when we start?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I agreed to furniture. I'm not joining your committee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just come and object, then. I'll give you the first turn; we need someone to get the meeting started.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 promises hall management and asks chair permission; A3 converts it to chairmanship, while A5 offers speaking priority to retain the objector.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 furniture assent enables A3 meeting reveal; B4 rejection causes A5 objector role rather than forced membership.

relationship.evidence: B4 refuses organisational commitment and A5 makes that objection a route to participation.

heightening.evidence: A5 expands B4 refusal into opening the meeting, but explains why the organiser needs someone in the final clause.

specificity.evidence: A1 noticeboard hall and A3 tenants meeting clearly locate a shared-building discussion.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 last clause explains the dependence the first-turn offer already enacts and could be cut.
